turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry we're a bit late, the parking was a nightmare and Niamh needed a feed in the car.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): You're grand, come on in. I'm Dr. Keane. What brought you in today?

[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): It's me, doctor, not the baby. Umm, I can't sleep even when she's fast asleep, and I keep crying over nothing. I'm six weeks after the delivery and I thought I'd be more myself, so I booked the appointment.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. Let me say that back. Six weeks postnatal, not sleeping even when the baby sleeps, and tearful. How long has the sleep been off?

[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Week one I could still drop off if she did. From the second week, err, so four weeks now, I lie awake going over the labour and the bottles and every little job. I'm exhausted with it too, drained all day, heavy in the arms and legs, the same four weeks.
[SEG0006] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She sleeps badly. I take Niamh into the spare room and she's still wide awake. I'm anxious about it, I'll be honest, I'm hardly sleeping myself from the worry.
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): He has that right. The room can be quiet as anything and I'm staring at the ceiling. It's not her noise, it's my head that won't switch off.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): The crying, how often is that happening?

[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): Nearly every day, err, for the last three weeks. Something tiny sets it off, the washing or the radio, and then I'm in floods for a long time. Not every hour, but most days, and it's heavy when it comes.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Under the tears, is the mood itself low?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): It is, yeah. Umm. Flat, like the colour's gone out of the day. I manage the feeds and the nappies, but there's no joy in it, and that's been the three weeks as well.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): I need to ask this directly. Any thoughts of hurting yourself?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): No. None at all. I've been desperate for a night's sleep but I have not thought of harming myself.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): And any thoughts of harming Niamh?
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): No, never, not for a second. I get a fright I might drop her when I'm clumsy from tiredness, but I would never hurt her.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright. No thoughts of harm to you or to her. How is the appetite?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. One day I'll eat the dinner, the next I'll push it round the plate, so I can't say it straight.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Does your heart race on you?
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): Sometimes, not really. One night I was crying and I counted it at 96, and then it settled, so I didn't chase it.
[SEG0020] person_4 (NURSE): I did her observations outside. Pulse is 96, blood pressure 122 over 78. She had mentioned that 96 to me in the corridor before we came in.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right so. Today's reading is 122 over 78, pulse 96. Any chest pain, shortness of breath, or headaches?
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): No chest pain, no shortness of breath, and no headaches. My mind is busy but nothing actually pains me.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): What about the eyes, or the skin, any rash or bother?
[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): No, nothing in the eyes and nothing on the skin.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): How did the tear heal?
[SEG0026] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The cut healed in five days. The midwife told us it looked perfect.

[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): That's true, five days and it was closed over. It was sore those days, then no weeping and no smell. I was watching for a slow heal, like my cousin had, and it never happened.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll have a look. Yes, the perineum is well healed, no redness and no gaping.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any operations in the past?
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): No, never had one. First baby, normal delivery, just that tear and nothing else.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Who's at home, and do you smoke?
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): Just the three of us in the house in Raheny, himself and me and Niamh. My mam calls in but she doesn't live with us. And I never smoked, not even one.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): What medicines are you taking?

[SEG0034] person_3 (PATIENT): Ferrous sulphate, two hundred milligrams by mouth once a day, for the low iron after the birth. I've been on it about five weeks, since I came home. It bungs me up, hard stools the whole time, so I skip Saturdays when his mother visits. The other days I take it, though if the night was desperate I might miss another, and I'm not fully sure.
[SEG0035] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She doesn't take the tablets on Sundays. I've checked the box of a Sunday night and it hasn't moved.
[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): Ah here, no. Sundays I take it with the dinner. It's Saturdays I leave out, not Sundays. I told you that.

[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me settle that. Ferrous sulphate two hundred milligrams once a day by mouth, you miss Saturdays and not Sundays, and you're unsure if another day slips. Constipation from the iron. Anything you stopped, or were offered and didn't take?

[SEG0038] person_3 (PATIENT): I stopped the Difene after the first week. That's the diclofenic, fifty milligrams by mouth three times a day, for the afterpains, and it burned my stomach so I knocked it on the head. They offered me zopiclone in the hospital to sleep and I never took it, not the once.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): So Difene is stopped, and the zopiclone was never taken. Any vomiting, or blood in the stool?
[SEG0040] person_3 (PATIENT): No vomiting, and no blood. It's only the constipation.

[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll summarise. Six weeks after the baby, low and tearful for three weeks, awake even when Niamh sleeps, exhausted, no thoughts of harm, and the tear healed. My impression is this may be postnatal depression, not only the brief blues, but that's provisional. I won't call it definite today.

[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll send you for a full blood count today, with the tiredness and the iron being hit and miss. If that count comes back low we might check the thyroid, otherwise not. I'm not starting a new medicine today.

[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll ask the public health nurse to call to the house this week. And I'll see you back here in two weeks. If you're no better at that visit we might refer you to the perinatal mental health team.

[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): If a thought of harming yourself or the baby appears before then, go to the hospital or ring the surgery, don't sit on it. Let him take one night feed so you can try to lie down, and keep the iron going apart from the Saturday.
[SEG0045] person_3 (PATIENT): I will. He can have the early feed and I'll stay on the iron bar Saturday.
[SEG0046] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll do the feed, yeah. And I'll stop mixing up Saturday and Sunday.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Reception has the blood form and they'll book the two weeks. Mind yourselves going out.

spec.situation: Mother six weeks after delivery, tearful, not sleeping even when the baby sleeps; partner present and anxious; denies harming herself or the baby when asked directly; support and follow-up planned.

traps.happens: The doctor asks about drug reactions. Variants (use ONE per encounter): (a) the patient says 'No, never, I have taken penicillin and everything' (no allergy); (b) the patient is unsure ('maybe the antibiotic or the painkiller, nobody told me which'); (c) a real allergy with the reaction described; (d) allergies are never asked.
traps.label_rule: (a) NO allergy entry: negative_findings 'Allergies' absent. (b) allergy with status uncertain, the substance as described, the reaction if said, plus an allergy_uncertain uncertainty. (c) allergy with the reaction. (d) nothing at all. NEVER list a medicine the patient has taken without a reaction as an allergy, and the plan must not prescribe a drug of a recorded allergy's family.

traps.happens: A caregiver or relative reports observations ('the cut healed in five days', 'she sleeps badly', 'he does not take the tablets on Sundays'); the patient agrees, disagrees or corrects one point. The nurse also reports a measurement that the patient mentioned before.
traps.label_rule: reported_by follows who said it. A healing cut that healed normally is a negative finding (no slow-healing wounds) or nothing, NOT a symptom. A disputed fact is recorded with certainty disputed or as an uncertainty. A correction replaces the earlier value (Saturday, not Sunday).

features: ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

bad.reason: Constipation from iron is supported, but duration of about 5 weeks is not stated for constipation.
bad.text: Constipation (category=gastrointestinal, status=present, duration=approximately 5 weeks, temporality=current, aggravating_factors=ferrous sulphate, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

bad.reason: Stopped Difene is supported, but generic was said as 'diclofenic,' not diclofenac.
bad.text: Difene (generic_name=diclofenac, dose=50 mg, route=oral, frequency=three times a day, duration=P1W, indication=afterpains, status=discontinued, reported_by=patient)

omissions.text: Low appetite/variable appetite: some days eats dinner, other days just pushes it around the plate.
Anhedonia/loss of joy: she manages feeds and nappies but 'there's no joy in it.'

Current medication adherence detail: ferrous sulphate causes hard stools/constipation and she deliberately skips Saturdays; there was a brief disagreement from family member incorrectly saying Sundays, corrected by patient and doctor.
Stopped medication adverse effect: diclofenac/Difene 50 mg PO three times daily was stopped after the first week because it burned her stomach.
Medicine offered but not taken: zopiclone was offered in hospital for sleep and she never took it at all.
Obstetric history: first baby, normal delivery, with just the tear and nothing else.
Plan: doctor is not starting any new medication today.
